standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the ring obtained by adjoining the root as a discrete valuation ring with the correct fraction field and ramification index.

standard_prerequisites.name: Tameness is preserved by composition of extensions of discrete valuation rings and inherited by subextensions
standard_prerequisites.use: Deduces tameness of L over K from tameness of the larger extension L' and from the fact that L is a subextension.

standard_prerequisites.name: Abhyankar's lemma: after adjoining a root of the uniformizer of exponent equal to the ramification index, the extension becomes formally smooth in the adic topology, hence unramified
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that each factor of the base change becomes unramified over the new base, which is condition (2).

core_obligations: Observe that the ring obtained from A by adjoining an e-th root of the uniformizer is a discrete valuation ring with ramification index e over A, and record that condition (3) trivially implies condition (2) (proof lines 34202-34210).

Prove that (2) implies (1): if L is contained in an extension which is unramified over the base extended by the root, then that larger extension is tamely ramified over A by the composition statement, and tameness descends to the subextension L (proof lines 34204-34207).

Assume (1) and set up the data: let B be the integral closure of A in L with maximal ideals indexed by i, let e_i be the ramification indices and let e_0 be their least common multiple, which is invertible in the residue field by tameness; then for a chosen multiple e of e_0 set the new base to be A adjoined the e-th root of the uniformizer (proof lines 34213-34221).

Write the base change of L as a product of fields and let the integral closures of A in those fields be considered; for a maximal ideal of one factor lying over a maximal ideal of B, apply Abhyankar's lemma to the corresponding extension and the chosen root extension to conclude that the map is formally smooth in the adic topology (proof lines 34222-34234).

Conclude from formal smoothness that the ramification index is one and the residue field extension is separable, so each factor is unramified over the new base; taking one factor gives condition (2) with e equal to the chosen multiple of e_0, which is condition (3) (proof lines 34234-34239).
proof_roadmap: Note that the root extension has the right ramification index and that (3) implies (2) trivially (proof lines 34202-34210).
From (2) deduce tameness of the larger extension by composition and of L by subextensions (proof lines 34204-34207).
From (1) build e_0 from the ramification indices over the maximal ideals of the integral closure, choose a multiple e and adjoin the e-th root of the uniformizer (proof lines 34213-34221).
Decompose the base change into fields, apply Abhyankar's lemma to each factor and conclude unramifiedness from formal smoothness, giving (3) (proof lines 34222-34239).
difficulty_reason: The statement gives three equivalent characterizations of tame ramification of a finite separable extension of the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring: tameness itself, containment in an extension that is unramified after adjoining a root of the uniformizer of exponent invertible in the residue field, and the same with the exponent running through all multiples of a fixed invertible e_0 (statement lines 34184-34199). The proof closes the cycle by three steps: the equivalence of the second and third conditions is immediate, the second implies tameness by the composition and subextension statements, and tameness implies the third by a construction in which the ramification indices over the maximal ideals of the integral closure give the exponent e_0, the base is extended by a root of the uniformizer, the base change is decomposed into fields, and Abhyankar's lemma together with formal smoothness produces the unramified factor (proof lines 34202-34239). The least common multiple step and the passage from formal smoothness to unramifiedness are the two technical points. The counted span refers five times to earlier results of this chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
